item.title: x-2026-10-09-rag-plain-english
item.description:
What is RAG, in plain English?
RAG stands for retrieval-augmented generation. In practice it means this:
→ Someone asks a question → The system finds the relevant parts of your documents → The AI writes an answer based on those parts
So instead of a chatbot guessing from general knowledge, it answers from your policies, manuals, contracts or product docs.
Sounds simple. Whether it works well depends heavily on your documents, which is why we suggest proving it first.
Our RAG proof of concept takes your real documents, turns them into a working prototype you can test, and ends with a clear go or no-go decision.

item.title: x-2026-10-12-loinix-trust
item.description:
Would you pay a stranger online before the job is done?
Most people wouldn't. That hesitation is what a good marketplace has to design around.
On Loinix, a UK marketplace we built, trust is built into every trade in three ways:
→ Trust scores give buyers and sellers a signal about who they are dealing with → Escrow payments hold the money until the work is complete → Real-time chat lets both sides agree details before anything is paid
None of these is a single feature on its own. Together they give people enough confidence to take the first step.

item.title: x-2026-10-13-clean-data
item.description:
Your AI is only as good as the spreadsheet it learns from.
It's tempting to think a more powerful model will fix messy results. Usually it won't. If customer records are duplicated, half-filled and scattered across three systems, any model will struggle.
Before any AI project, try this:
→ Remove duplicates. The same customer listed twice looks like two customers to a machine. → Fill in missing fields. Blank dates, categories and statuses leave the model guessing. → Agree on one source of truth. Decide which system holds the real version of each record.
None of this is glamorous. All of it makes AI results more reliable, and your reports cleaner too.
